newsitem.title: USA: Varian to cut 115 semiconductor plant workers.
newsitem.headline: Varian to cut 115 semiconductor plant workers.

text.p: Varian Associates Inc. said Thursday it is cutting about 115 jobs at its semiconductor equipment factories in Gloucester, Mass., and Palo Alto, Calif., due to slow demand.

The move trims employment at the factories, which make machines used to manufacture computer chips and other semiconductor devices, by about 6 percent, and cuts the company's work force by less than 2 percent.
Varian, a diversified company, said the semiconductor industry continues to suffer from overcapacity and price cuts, resulting in lower demand for new chip-making equipment.
About 85 of the workers affected are at the Gloucester plant, which had a similar reduction in mid-August, with the balance at the Palo Alto unit.
Palo Alto-based Varian said the workers will receive severance payments and outplacement assistance.
Varian has core businesses in health care systems, semiconductor equipment and analytical instruments.
Varian's stock fell 62.5 cents to $47.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
